volume: Burke, Kenneth. 1945. A Grammar of Motives. New York: Prentice-Hall (rpt. Berkeley: University of California Press, 1969).
source: Aggregation across 14 deep-unit JSONs (GM-00 through GM-13) + Index pp. 540-551 + Phase 0 cite-presence data

tier_definitions.A: Cited in >=3 chapters OR receives sustained-analysis treatment (>=2 pages of continuous exegesis)
tier_definitions.B: Cited in 2 chapters OR receives illustrative-block treatment (1-2 paragraphs of substantive engagement)

philosophers.name: Aristotle
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Act' (Aristotle and Aquinas), book pp. 227-274; also pp. 252-262 (act and potency); index lemma pp. 519-520 enumerates >25 sub-loci
philosophers.pentad_term_burke_features_them_for: Act (with secondary purpose-stress via final cause)
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Aristotle is Burke's preferred lexicon for act-philosophy: hylomorphism, act-potency, four causes, entelechy, and the energeia/dynamis pairing are mined as the substrate from which all dramatistic act-vocabulary radiates; Burke repeatedly returns to Nicomachean Ethics, Metaphysics, Physics, Rhetoric, and Poetics for technical terms he then translates into pentadic apparatus.

philosophers.name: Aquinas
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Act' co-protagonist with Aristotle, pp. 227-232 and pp. 247-262 (realist-family/nominalist-aggregate; actus-status pp. 41-43); index lemma p. 519
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Burke treats Aquinas as the medium through which Aristotelian act-philosophy enters Christian theology, especially the actus/status doctrine, the realist understanding of substance, and the linking of grace to act; the Summa is treated as a structural exemplar of dialectical-dramatic terminology.

philosophers.name: Spinoza
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Scene (Philosophic Schools)', pp. 137-152 (extended philosophical-school treatment); also pp. 24-26 (contextual paradox), pp. 50, pp. 72-77 (pantheism)
philosophers.pentad_term_burke_features_them_for: Scene (materialism transcended-via-pantheism; substance defined by contextual placement)
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Spinoza is Burke's paradigm of scene-philosophy at its most dialectically refined: substance=that-by-which-defined-by-what-it-is-not, the Ethics' active/passive verb-structure, the three forms of knowledge, and the pantheist circumference are excavated as Scene-term machinery; Burke aligns Spinoza's negation-formula with his own concept of dialectical substance.

philosophers.name: Plato
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Dialectic in General', pp. 402-443 (Socratic transcendence pp. 420-430); also pp. 173 (Justice), 421-423 (Jowett), 425 (Platonic love), 427 (Phaedrus)
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Plato is the paradigm of Socratic-dialectical transcendence: the upward path from particulars through stages of merging-and-dividing toward an ultimate-term is read by Burke as the dialectical archetype of all motive-theory; the Phaedrus and Symposium furnish Burke's image of the dialectician-as-statesman.

philosophers.name: Hegel
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Agent in General' (idealism after Kant pp. 198-200); also pp. 46-47, pp. 200-204 (philosophy of history), pp. 281-282 (Marx-reversal), pp. 312 (rationalism)
philosophers.pentad_term_burke_features_them_for: Agent (collective-historical Geist) + Dialectic (Aufhebung as merger-and-division paradigm)
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Hegel furnishes the dialectical syntax that Burke generalizes as merger-and-division (the four-master-tropes apparatus is partly a Hegel-derivative); the cunning-of-reason, Insofern, and World-Spirit are recoded into pentadic ratios; Marx's inversion of Hegel is itself thematized as a dialectical move.

philosophers.name: Kant
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Agent in General' pp. 185-197 (philosophy of); pp. 192-197 (moral transcendence); pp. 188 (intuition); pp. 198 (idealism after Kant); pp. 404-405 (on merger)
philosophers.pentad_term_burke_features_them_for: Agent (transcendental subject as Agent-idealization); also Purpose (categorical imperative)
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Kant is the hinge from scene-philosophy to agent-philosophy: the transcendental apparatus (forms of intuition, categories, schematism, the noumenal-phenomenal split) is reframed as the philosophical-school featuring Agent; the antinomies pre-figure Burke's own antinomies-of-definition; the Critique of Pure Reason and the moral-philosophy are mined for ratio-structure.

philosophers.name: Hobbes
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Scene', pp. 131-137 (Hobbes as materialist; Leviathan; Endeavor/Appetite/Aversion); references in Constitutions chapter
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Hobbes inaugurates the modern scene-philosophy lineage: a thoroughgoing materialism that reduces motive to motion (Endeavor-Appetite-Aversion); Burke treats Leviathan as a constitutional-political application of scene-philosophy in which the sovereign is the personified scenic ground.

philosophers.name: Leibniz
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Leibniz figures as transitional between scene and agent: the monad is read as proto-agent (each monad an internally-driven principle); pre-established harmony is treated as a dialectical solution to mind-body that bequeaths the calculus-of-pure-thought lineage Burke ties to logical positivism.

philosophers.name: Marx
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Agent' pp. 209-214 (dramatist grammar for Marxism; class-action); pp. 200-202 (dialectical materialism); pp. 215-218 (class-concept); pp. 281-282 (Hegel-reversal)
philosophers.pentad_term_burke_features_them_for: Agent (collective-class agent); scene-act ratio via dialectical materialism
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Burke supplies a dramatist grammar for Marxism: class is read as a dramatistic agent (not a sociological aggregate), the Manifesto as a representative anecdote, and dialectical materialism as a scene-stressed dialectic that nonetheless requires an agent-term (proletariat) to consummate; the Hegel-inversion is dramatized as a pentadic shift.

philosophers.name: William James
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Agency and Purpose' pp. 62-66 (act as locus of motives; way of creation); pp. 275-277, 282-283 (pragmatism); pp. 286 (cash-value); pp. 287-298 (mystic moment)
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: James is Burke's chief twentieth-century interlocutor for the act-as-locus-of-motives thesis; the pragmatist circumference, the two principles of truth, and the Varieties of Religious Experience are read as agency-purpose philosophy par excellence; Burke deploys James as the rhetorical pivot from scene to act.

philosophers.name: Bergson
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Agency and Purpose' pp. 295-296 (negation; purposiveness); pp. 152, 412 (Creative Evolution)
philosophers.pentad_term_burke_features_them_for: Act (elan vital as creative-act principle); Agency
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Bergson is enlisted for the purposiveness-in-the-negative theme and for treating biological-creative process as scene-act fusion; Creative Evolution is cross-read with Darwin to extract a counter-mechanist motive-vocabulary.

philosophers.name: Plotinus
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Antinomies' and 'Agency and Purpose' pp. 293-294 (Neo-Platonist purpose); pp. 30, 34 (index)
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Plotinus is the Neo-Platonist exemplar of purpose-philosophy: emanation downward from the One and ascent of soul back to the One is treated by Burke as the archetypal purpose-trajectory, with Plotinus serving as bridge between Plato and Christian mystical theology.

philosophers.name: Darwin
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Scene' pp. 152-158 (Darwin's naturalism); pp. 291 (mysticism and materialism); pp. 431-432
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Darwin is the modern materialist scene-philosopher; natural selection furnishes Burke's example of a scene-act ratio in which the agent (organism) is wholly scene-derived; Origin of Species is read as a representative anecdote whose generalization Burke contests.

philosophers.name: Lucretius
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Scene' pp. 159-164 (Epicurean materialism); pp. 162 (De Rerum Natura); pp. 160 (atoms swerving)
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Lucretius furnishes the Epicurean variant of scene-philosophy: atoms-and-void plus the clinamen (swerve) as the residual proto-agency embedded in materialist scene; Burke contrasts Lucretius's Epicurean materialism with Stoic providential materialism.

philosophers.name: Coleridge
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'The Problem of the Intrinsic' pp. 470-471 (criticism of); cross-chapter pp. 14, 34, 192, 233, 296, 299, 325, 338, 359-360, 368-371, 408, 411-412; sustained 'pantisocracy' analysis
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Coleridge is Burke's primary literary-theoretical interlocutor: Biographia Literaria's primary/secondary imagination, the doctrine of organic form, the pantisocracy project, and Coleridge's dialectic of negation all furnish Burke with a Romantic-poetic vocabulary that translates onto pentadic ratios; the Keats and Moore chapters extend Coleridgean reading-methods.

philosophers.name: Santayana
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Santayana receives a full philosophical-schools treatment as a hybrid: skeptical-materialist scene (animal faith) plus Platonist essences, yielding a doubled grammar that Burke reads as the ideal mid-twentieth-century scene-agent attempt at integration.

philosophers.name: Korzybski
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Act' pp. 238-241 (concept of action; semantics); pp. 57, 173, 247, 251, 293, 317, 440, 511 (cross-chapter); appendix D critique
philosophers.pentad_term_burke_features_them_for: Act (general-semantics critique; structural-differential as a reductive anecdote)
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Korzybski is Burke's running critical foil: the Structural Differential is treated as a non-representative anecdote that misrepresents meaning by reducing it to a mechanical apparatus; Burke nonetheless adopts Korzybski's emphasis on terminological awareness and his critique of identity-A=A logic.

philosophers.name: Berkeley
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Berkeley is featured as the British-empiricist passage from Locke's representationalism to subjective idealism; esse est percipi reframes the agent as constitutive of perceived scene; Burke reads the divine perceiver as a transcendental rescue from solipsism.

philosophers.name: Hume
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Agent' pp. 181-184 (skepticism; on cause and effect); pp. 182 (experience); pp. 186, 415
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Hume is the empiricist pivot: causation as customary expectation, the bundle-theory of self, and the Treatise's destabilization of substance-vocabulary are treated as preparation for Kant's transcendental rescue.

philosophers.name: G. H. Mead
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Act' pp. 236-238 (vocal gesture; biologism); also pp. 279 (Mead's biologism); Philosophy of the Act referenced
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Mead supplies Burke with the social-act doctrine in which symbolic communication (vocal gesture) is constitutive of the self; Mind, Self, and Society and Philosophy of the Act anchor Burke's dramatism in pragmatist social-psychology.

philosophers.name: Augustine
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Agency and Purpose' pp. 142-144 (cross-reference); index pp. 519
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Augustine is the patristic exemplar of the Christianized purpose-philosophy (peregrinatio toward God); the Confessions' narrative arc is treated as a literary-theological purpose-trajectory.

philosophers.name: Locke
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Container and Thing Contained' pp. 22-23 (Essay); cross-ref pp. 177, 468
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Locke's Essay Concerning Human Understanding is Burke's reference-point for the representational theory of ideas; the tabula rasa is read as a scene-stressed account of agent-formation that prepares the British-empiricist sequence Berkeley-Hume.

philosophers.name: Duns Scotus
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Scotus supplies the haecceitas-doctrine that Burke uses as a counterpart to Aristotelian universals; the individuating principle is treated as a dialectical move within the realist-family of substance-terms.

philosophers.name: Windelband
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Antinomies' and 'Scope' pp. 70, 255 (history of philosophy as source)
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Windelband's history of philosophy is Burke's principal source-text for the systematic-school taxonomy organizing Part II; Burke borrows the idealism/realism/nominalism/materialism partition.

philosophers.name: I. A. Richards
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Richards is Burke's contemporary new-critical interlocutor; the directional-substance discussion and the synecdochic representation-doctrine engage Principles of Literary Criticism as a co-text against which Burke positions the pentad.

philosophers.name: Wordsworth
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Symbolic Action in a Poem by Keats' p. 246, 475; sonnets cited; cross-ref pp. 8
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Wordsworth supplies illustrative-block instances for Romantic agent/scene-agent ratios; the sonnets are mined as compact pentadic exemplars.

philosophers.name: Rousseau
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Rousseau is a constitutional/political reference: the social contract and the natural-man trope furnish background for Burke's Dialectic-of-Constitutions chapter.

philosophers.name: Descartes
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Scene' p. 55 (substance-definition); pp. 146-147 (Cartesian dualism); pp. 177, 225, 311 (Discourse on Method)
philosophers.pentad_term_burke_features_them_for: Scene-Agent split (mind-body dualism as paradigmatic antinomy)
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Descartes is the canonical case of mind-body dualism that Burke reads as a dramatistic disjoining of agent (res cogitans) from scene (res extensa); the cogito is treated as agent-philosophy in radical form.

philosophers.name: Fichte
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Fichte furnishes the radicalization of Kant's transcendental subject into the absolute-positing I; Burke treats this as the high-water mark of agent-philosophy before Hegel's dialectical synthesis.

philosophers.name: Schelling
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Schelling figures as transitional between Fichte's agent-idealism and Hegel's dialectical idealism; the philosophy of Nature is read as scene-reabsorption of agent.

philosophers.name: Schopenhauer
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Schopenhauer's World as Will is treated as a voluntarist-agent variant of post-Kantian idealism in which the agent-term is metaphysically primary.

philosophers.name: Nietzsche
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Nietzsche is the great debunker whose genealogical method Burke treats as a reductive operation on motive-terms.

philosophers.name: Engels
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Engels co-figures with Marx in the dialectical-materialist pairing; the Communist Manifesto is treated as a representative-anecdote text with Engels as Marx's pentadic partner.

philosophers.name: Lenin
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Container' p. 13; Ch. 'Act' p. 174; Ch. 'Agent' pp. 200, 201, 205, 207, 208 (Materialism and Empirio-Criticism; State and Revolution; What Is To Be Done)
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Lenin furnishes the operationalization of Marxism as revolutionary practice; the vanguard-party is read as a particular Agency-form attached to the Marxian Agent-term.

philosophers.name: Trotsky
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Trotsky is invoked alongside Lenin as a Marxist tactician whose dispute with Stalin Burke reads in pentadic terms.

philosophers.name: Stalin
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Stalin appears as the historical instance of socialism-as-monetary-system, in critical contrast to the more dramatistically supple early Marx-Engels.

philosophers.name: Freud
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Ch. 'Dialectic in General' pp. 305, 313, 431, 432 (Totem and Taboo; Group Psychology); cross-ref pp. 71, 265
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Freud is treated as a modern motive-theorist whose psychoanalytic vocabulary (ego, super-ego, libido, primal horde) is read as a dramatistic agency-mechanism; Burke critically positions psychoanalysis within his broader survey of reductive motive-vocabularies.

philosophers.name: Dewey
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Dewey is the second-generation pragmatist whose instrumentalism Burke treats as the explicit agency-philosophy paired with James's earlier purpose-stressed pragmatism.

philosophers.name: Peirce
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Peirce is treated as the originating pragmatist whose theory of signs furnishes a semiotic backbone for the agency-purpose dialectic.

philosophers.name: Bentham
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Pp. 162, 183, 284-285 (Table of the Springs of Action)
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Bentham's table of motive-springs is Burke's exemplar of a reductive motive-taxonomy that nonetheless prefigures dramatistic terminology.

philosophers.name: Bonaventura
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Bonaventura supplies an additional medieval data-point for the Christianized purpose-philosophy, alongside Aquinas and Augustine.

philosophers.name: Avicenna (Ibn-Sina)
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Avicenna features in the medieval-Aristotelian backstory that prepares Aquinas's appropriation.

philosophers.name: William of Occam
philosophers.pentad_term_burke_features_them_for: Methodology (Occam's Razor as a reductive-anecdote example) + Agent (nominalism)
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Occam supplies Burke's running reference for the law of parsimony; nominalism is treated as a permanent dialectical pole opposed to realism, with both poles necessary to dramatism.

philosophers.name: Bréhier
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Bréhier is Burke's principal scholarly source for medieval-philosophy details, alongside Gilson.

philosophers.name: Etienne Gilson
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Gilson supplies the Neo-Thomist scholarly authority for Burke's Aquinas reading.

philosophers.name: Heraclitus
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Heraclitus is the pre-Socratic exemplar of process-philosophy, treated briefly as background for dialectical motion.

philosophers.name: Democritus
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Democritus is the ancient origin-point of the atomistic scene-lineage that runs through Lucretius to Hobbes and modern materialism.

philosophers.name: Zeno of Elea
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Zeno's paradoxes furnish Burke's example of dialectic in its earliest aporetic form.

philosophers.name: Thales
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Thales appears as ancestral Ionian nature-philosopher.

philosophers.name: Stoics (Marcus Aurelius, Epictetus, Seneca)
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Stoicism is the providential-materialist counterpart to Epicurean materialism; Aurelius and Epictetus furnish the late-antique paradigm of scene-stressed yet morally-active philosophy.

philosophers.name: Galileo
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Galileo is the inaugurator of mathematized scene-philosophy that opens the modern scientific-reductive lineage.

philosophers.name: Heisenberg
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle furnishes Burke's modern-physics datum for probability-as-substance.

philosophers.name: Bridgman
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Bridgman's operationalism furnishes a contemporary example of agency-philosophy reducing meaning to procedure.

philosophers.name: Kurt Lewin
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Lewin's psychological field-theory contributes to Burke's modern motive-vocabulary survey.

philosophers.name: Andras Angyal
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Pp. 31, 469-470 (Foundations for a Science of Personality)
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Angyal's holistic personality-science is invoked in the Intrinsic chapter as a sympathetic modern parallel to dramatism.

philosophers.name: Wilhelm Reich
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Reich is one of Burke's psychoanalytic data-points alongside Freud and Jung.

philosophers.name: Jung
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Jung supplies the collective-unconscious doctrine that Burke reads as a quasi-tribal Agent-term.

philosophers.name: Frank Hyneman Knight
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Knight's economics-as-ethics yields the tendency-concept Burke uses for partial Acts.

philosophers.name: Veblen
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Veblen anchors Burke's institutional-economic backdrop, though no sustained passage; primarily an allusional figure.

philosophers.name: Cicero
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Cicero appears as background rhetorical reference.

philosophers.name: Matthew Arnold
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Arnold is invoked as Victorian humanist counterpoint.

philosophers.name: Thurman Arnold
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Arnold's reduction of social relations into psychiatric metaphor exemplifies a non-representative anecdote.

philosophers.name: Lovejoy (Arthur)
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Lovejoy's Great Chain of Being is Burke's history-of-ideas reference for substance-chain doctrines.

philosophers.name: Otto Neurath
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: Pp. 410-411, 431, 510 (isotypes; Foundations of the Social Sciences)
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Neurath's isotypes furnish Burke's prime example of quantitative-reductive representation contrasted with dramatistic representation.

philosophers.name: Edmund Burke (the political theorist)
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: P. 359 (Coleridge on Edmund Burke); also p. 359-360
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Edmund Burke is invoked (via Coleridge) as ancestor of conservative-constitutional reasoning, distinct from Kenneth Burke the author.

philosophers.name: Adam Smith
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Smith anchors Burke's discussion of capitalist-motive sceneography.

philosophers.name: Machiavelli
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Machiavelli supplies the realpolitik tactical idiom Burke uses to set up the scene-act ratio.

philosophers.name: Hugo Black
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Black furnishes a contemporary legal-constitutional example.

philosophers.name: Aeschylus
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Aeschylus furnishes the poiema-pathema-mathema triad that Burke embeds in dramatistic motive-analysis.

philosophers.name: Sophists
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: The Sophists furnish the rhetorical counter-position to Plato's idealist Justice.

philosophers.name: Theophrastus
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Theophrastus supplies the proto-typological character-vocabulary related to humour-characters.

philosophers.name: Avicebron
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Avicebron supplies a Jewish medieval data-point for the agent-philosophy lineage between Plotinus and Aquinas.

philosophers.name: Pascal
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Pascal contributes a Christian-existential motive-instance contrasted with rationalist Descartes.

philosophers.name: Charles Beard
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Beard's economic-interpretation of the US Constitution informs Burke's Dialectic-of-Constitutions analysis.

philosophers.name: James Mark Baldwin
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: P. 131 (Dictionary of Philosophy and Psychology — Burke's principal reference work)
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Baldwin's Dictionary of Philosophy and Psychology is Burke's standing reference work for school-definitions; treated as a tacit authority throughout the philosophical-schools chapters.

philosophers.name: Houston Peterson
philosophers.primary_discussion_locus: P. 266 (One Mighty Torrent: the Drama of Biography)
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Peterson's biographical-drama anthology furnishes a representative-anecdote about life-as-drama.

philosophers.name: Carlyle
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Carlyle's hero-cult is a Romantic-historicist Agent-philosophy variant.

philosophers.name: Marc Aurelius
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Marcus Aurelius is Burke's representative individual of late-antique Stoicism.

philosophers.name: Epictetus
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Epictetus furnishes the Stoic dichotomy-of-control as a proto-pentadic ratio of agent and scene.

philosophers.name: Epicurus
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Epicurus furnishes the second great Hellenistic materialism, paired with Stoicism.

philosophers.name: Lewis Feuer
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Feuer supplies contemporary philosophy-of-science backdrop.

philosophers.name: Marquis de Laplace
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Laplace anchors Burke's reference for Newtonian determinism.

philosophers.name: Newton
philosophers.burke_exegetical_move: Newton represents the classical-mechanical scene against which modern indeterminacy is set.
